record.original_question: Determine whether there exist two permutation patterns whose avoidance counts switch relative order more than once, and in particular whether two patterns can switch places infinitely often as n grows.

evidence.quote: It is still unknown whether such a switch occurs twice or more for any pair of patterns, but Stankova and West conjecture [42, Conjecture 2] that this does not happen.
They also make the weaker conjecture that for any pair of patterns σ and τ there is an N such that either Avσ(n) < Avτ(n) for all n > N or else the opposite inequality holds for all n > N.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For permutations, given a pattern $\sigma$ (a permutation of $\{1,2,\dots,k\}$), say that a permutation $\pi$ of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ avoids $\sigma$ if there is no subsequence $\pi(i_1),\pi(i_2),\dots,\pi(i_k)$ with $i_1<i_2<\cdots<i_k$ whose entries are in the same relative order as $\sigma(1),\sigma(2),\dots,\sigma(k)$. Let $\mathrm{Av}_\sigma(n)$ denote the number of permutations of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$ that avoid $\sigma$.

For a pair of patterns $\sigma,\tau$, say that a "switch" occurs at $n$ if the strict inequality between $\mathrm{Av}_\sigma(n)$ and $\mathrm{Av}_\tau(n)$ at $n$ is the opposite of the strict inequality at $n-1$ (with both inequalities strict).

Determine whether the following holds:

(a) (Strong form.) For every pair of patterns $\sigma,\tau$, at most one switch occurs as $n$ ranges over the positive integers.

(b) (Weak form.) For every pair of patterns $\sigma,\tau$, there exists $N$ such that either $\mathrm{Av}_\sigma(n)<\mathrm{Av}_\tau(n)$ for all $n>N$ or $\mathrm{Av}_\sigma(n)>\mathrm{Av}_\tau(n)$ for all $n>N$ (equivalently, only finitely many switches occur).

In particular, can two patterns switch places infinitely often as $n\to\infty$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any resolution of the Stankova–West conjectures on whether avoidance counts of two patterns can switch order more than once or infinitely often. Surveys and follow-up literature on pattern avoidance still refer to this as a conjecture, with no announced proof or counterexample found.

status_evidence.title: Stankova's research works
status_evidence.snippet: Stankova and West have conjectured for the general permutation case whether the cardinality classes can be ordered asymptotically.
status_evidence.claim: The asymptotic ordering question of Stankova–West remains stated as a conjecture in the literature.
